bullets.title: Jodorowsky’s Dune
bullets.note:
Sometimes, you can learn a lot from failures, which is why I (and [Nassim Taleb](https://tim.blog/2023/09/07/nassim-nicholas-taleb-scott-patterson/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit#content)) like the book [_What I Learned Losing a Million Dollars_](https://www.audible.com/pd/What-I-Learned-Losing-a-Million-Dollars-Audiobook/B00NC8XVVC), for example. _Jodorowsky's Dune_ is the hilarious telling of a spectacularly bold failure. My favorite parts are the highlights of lessons learned, as well as the stories of how team members later helped create spectacular successes (e.g., the Alien in [_Alien_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alien_(film))). The later diaspora of talent reminded me of the incredible General Magic startup story, which you can [learn about here](https://youtu.be/5M5SJ5u0Ke4?t=503).  
​  
To give you a taste, here are a few quotes from the titular director, Alejandro Jodorowsky:  
​  
​_“I ask of film what most North Americans ask of psychedelic drugs.”  
​  
“Most directors make films with their eyes; I make films with my balls.”  
​  
“I will hire the chef of this restaurant, and you will eat, as here, every day.” (This was_ [_his pitch to get Orson Welles_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Harkonnen#Cancelled_1970s_film) _to act in_ Dune_.)  
​  
“One day, someone showed me a glass of water that was half full. And he said, ‘Is it half full or half empty?’ So I drank the water. No more problem.”  
​  
​_At a minimum, check out the trailer [here](https://youtu.be/m0cJNR8HEw0?si=lCVdAUDWYkI4bJJ3).

bullets.title: How to Heal the Anxious Self
bullets.note: I had the pleasure of sitting down with poet David Whyte [for an interview](https://tim.blog/2024/12/05/david-whyte/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit#content) a few months ago, and he proved as wonderful in person as he is on the page. During our conversation, he read from his most recent work, [_Consolations II_](https://davidwhyte.com/store/book/consolations-ii/). Now, I have a dog-eared hardcover copy by my bedside. It’s indispensable. No matter the challenge, dream, mystery, or feeling of stuckness, he has a poem or essay within that will help you. I’ve recently been rereading one of his essays in particular, and David kindly agreed to allow me to share it with you [on my blog](https://tim.blog/2025/04/09/how-to-heal-the-anxious-self-david-whyte/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit#content).
